description: Original disposable passages and manually specified expected destinations. No genuine learner records or production corpus.

passages.title: Working directory and relative paths
passages.text: The shell working directory is the directory from which a relative path is resolved. pwd prints the current working directory. A filename can exist elsewhere while a command reports file not found.

passages.title: Node and browser capabilities
passages.text: Node executes JavaScript outside a browser page. document is undefined because the DOM document object belongs to a browser environment. A shell launches node with a filename; JavaScript statements belong in a JavaScript runtime.

passages.title: A returned value differs from displayed output
passages.text: A function return supplies a value to the caller. console.log displays output and normally returns undefined. An assignment receives the returned value, not the visible message.

passages.title: Sorting numbers in JavaScript
passages.text: The default array sort converts values to strings. Numeric sorting can supply a comparator such as (a,b) => a-b. sort mutates the array; copying before sorting preserves original order.

passages.title: HTTP status is a response property
passages.text: HTTP 404 is a received response status. It differs from a DNS lookup error or a connection timeout. The response can contain headers and a body even when the status indicates an application error.

passages.title: Curl exit status and HTTP failure
passages.text: A received HTTP 404 does not necessarily make curl exit nonzero. --fail-with-body changes how curl reports HTTP failure. Inspect the process exit status separately from the HTTP status.

passages.title: PKCE protects a public OAuth client
passages.text: PKCE uses a code verifier and code challenge to bind authorization to the client that began the flow. A browser client must not embed a client secret. Inspect redirect URI and state as separate concerns.

passages.title: Regex flags and case
passages.text: JavaScript regular expressions can use the i flag for case insensitive matching. Engine dialects differ; a JavaScript expression is not necessarily PCRE or Python syntax. Test a small representative input.

passages.title: Unicode representations and offsets
passages.text: A displayed grapheme can contain several code points. JavaScript string offsets count UTF-16 code units. NFC normalization can combine a letter and combining accent; equal-looking text need not have identical bytes.

passages.title: Dictionary lookup with a default
passages.text: Python dict.get(key, default) returns a value or a fallback for a missing key. Indexing with brackets raises KeyError when the key is absent. A stored None is not the same condition as an absent key.

passages.title: Lists preserve ordered positions
passages.text: A Python list has ordered elements indexed from zero. A missing position raises IndexError. Mutating a list and producing a new list have different effects on other references.

passages.title: A commit identifies a Git snapshot
passages.text: A Git commit identifies a repository snapshot and parent history. A commit does not prove that a program executed successfully. Pin a full commit SHA and path when referring to exact source.

passages.title: Compare selected Git versions
passages.text: git diff compares chosen versions or the working tree. A diff shows changes in source, not why the learner made them. Save the reasoning separately from the patch.

passages.title: Effect cleanup and stale requests
passages.text: A React effect can start a network request and clean up when its dependencies change. AbortController cancels supported requests. A stale response needs an identity or ordering guard before updating current state.

passages.title: React state and object mutation
passages.text: A React state update should produce a new object when changing an object value. const prevents rebinding a variable; it does not freeze nested object properties. A stale closure can retain an earlier value.

passages.title: SQL NULL is not an ordinary equal value
passages.text: SQL NULL represents missing or unknown information. Use IS NULL rather than equality to test it. Three valued logic affects WHERE conditions and aggregate functions can ignore NULL values.

passages.title: Join rows through an explicit relation
passages.text: A SQL join combines rows using a chosen condition. Duplicate matching keys can multiply output rows. A left join retains unmatched left rows with NULL values from the right side.

passages.title: Revision guards prevent lost updates
passages.text: Compare and swap uses an expected revision before writing a changed record. A conflict retains the independent draft. Retrying an uncertain operation uses its original identity and payload.

passages.title: Exact passages retain a version
passages.text: An exact passage points to its rendition, section, part and UTF-16 offsets. Editing the current article must not move an earlier quotation onto different words. Canonical text is separate from visual line wrapping.

passages.title: Browser storage is not server acknowledgement
passages.text: localStorage retains text in one browser origin subject to quota and deletion. A local draft is not a server receipt. Persistent browser storage does not remove the need for an independent backup.

passages.title: Include HTTP response headers
passages.text: curl -i includes response headers along with the response body.

passages.title: Request HTTP metadata only
passages.text: curl -I requests a HEAD response; it is different from printing a GET response with headers.

passages.title: Map keyed collection
passages.text: The JavaScript Map constructor creates a keyed collection. Keys can be objects and iteration follows insertion order.

passages.title: Array map transformation
passages.text: Array map creates a new array from callback results for present elements. It is distinct from a keyed collection constructor.

passages.title: Nullish fallback
passages.text: The nullish coalescing operator uses its right operand only for null or undefined. It preserves zero and empty strings.

passages.title: Logical OR fallback
passages.text: Logical OR can choose a fallback for any falsy left operand, including zero or an empty string.

passages.title: Dictionary get method
passages.text: The exact Python method name offers a default when the key is absent.

passages.title: Copying source text
passages.text: Copy a source code example without display line numbers. Copying does not execute the program. The copied text should match what was shown.

passages.title: TCP connection is not an application response
passages.text: TCP provides a byte stream between connected endpoints. A listening socket differs from an established connection. Application protocols interpret the bytes.

passages.title: A digest identifies captured bytes
passages.text: A SHA-256 digest can compare captured file bytes. The digest does not prove ownership, successful execution or an understanding of the file. A repository reference alone is not byte verification.
